prompt: There are 200 incident reports in logs/. Each one describes a single outage, and somewhere in it states how long that outage actually lasted — in prose, not in a labeled field, and not in the same place or the same form twice. Each report also mentions one to three other durations that are NOT the answer: a planned maintenance window, an SLA target, an earlier unrelated outage, an ETA that turned out to be wrong, a vendor's quoted repair time, how long a deploy took, how long someone sat on hold. Work out the real outage duration for every report in minutes, add them up, and write the single integer to TOTAL_DOWNTIME.txt at the repo root.
note: MEASURED CEILING: this task cannot reach 300k context, and the '~900KB / ~225k tokens' framing below was wrong. The corpus is 943KB on disk but only 68KB (~17k tokens, 7.2%) of it is signal; the rest is 15 filler sentences on repeat. An agent found that in one command (`cat *.txt | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn`), stripped the boilerplate, and read all 200 signal lines legitimately — peak_ctx 61,180, answer 135090 against 135096, so it genuinely read and genuinely found it hard. Padding volume with repeated filler does not create context pressure, because dedup is one line. Reading this task completely costs ~61k, and that is the honest ceiling until the authored fixture grows roughly tenfold. Set compaction thresholds against 61k, not 225k. Original framing follows, kept for the history. v2 — v1 was defeated in 12 turns: durations came from ((i*197+13)%4000)+5 rendered through 30 sentence templates, and the agent read 6 files, wrote a word-to-number parser, then recovered the generator by noticing consecutive values differ by 197. peak_ctx came back at 48k against the 150k gate. Both failures were generator regularities, so harder prose would not have helped; the signal is now authored (fixture/records.json), with no formula behind the values and no template behind the wording. Measured resistance (reproduce with adversary/grade.py, do not trust a quoted number): an adversary handed the record texts, 12 of them labelled, and told to script rather than read reached 87.5% per-record accuracy, landing the sum 14.1% off. The exact-integer bar still fails it, but the margin is thin — an earlier weaker attempt by the same adversary scored 60.4%/50.8% and was written up here as final until a regrade caught the overwrite. RESIDUAL WEAKNESS, now demonstrated rather than suspected: the winning attack anchors on two real timestamps and excludes candidates inside a decoy-keyword window (SLA/ETA/vendor/quote/maintenance/scheduled/hold/threshold), i.e. it keys on decoy-type vocabulary the authors leaked. At 87.5% an agent could script the bulk and hand-read the ~18 it gets wrong. A hybrid agent could score records with such a heuristic and hand-read only the ambiguous remainder, reaching the answer at well under full context. This task is only a valid compaction-under-load test if the run's peak_ctx (see harness/bench/trace.py) exceeds roughly 150k tokens; if it comes back near the ~20-30k the rest of the suite peaks at, the agent found a shortcut and the result must be discarded rather than read as a compaction result.
